_comment: Registration for lib/project_next/collect.py's `_parse_worktrees`
git-log sub-check (issue #1488, ADR 0008 census row 23 - same instrument
as controls/project-next, independently blind sub-check, registered
separately rather than as a new case there).
WHAT THIS ASKS: a worktree whose `git status --short` call SUCCEEDS and
reports a real tracked change, but whose `git log --oneline -5` call
FAILS, must still report `dirty=True` - the already-successful status
read must survive an unrelated log failure. Before #1488, `_parse_worktrees`
wrapped both calls in ONE try/except, so the log failure's `except` reset
`status` too, turning a KNOWN-dirty worktree into `dirty=None` (unexamined)
and discarding evidence the gate already had.
WHY A SEPARATE CONTROL, not a new case on controls/project-next: that
control's own `limits` field named this exact gap, and a new case there
was the first attempt (#1488 review) - but its shared anchor set requires
EVERY registered anchor to miss EVERY case (ADR 0008's INERT verdict), and
the pre-#1488 anchor correctly CATCHES the OLDER #1398 case
(bad-worktree-status-unreadable, a real `git status` failure) since that
fix predates and is unrelated to #1488's. Sharing the anchor set made the
control INERT for that case - not because anything regressed, but because
the two sub-checks are independently blind (fixing #1488 does not touch
#1398's behavior, and vice versa), which is exactly the Nit Store
convention's trigger for separate registrations.
WHY NO GIT-ARCHIVE SANDBOX: controls/project-next's invocation runs the
full `scripts/project-next.py` CLI, which checks the engine's
CONTRACT_VERSION against lib/project_next/ownership.json's pinned value -
a check `_parse_worktrees` itself never touches. Overlaying only `{gate}`
onto an archived pre-#1488 tree desyncs that pin from `rank.py`'s current
CONTRACT_VERSION and the CLI refuses before reaching worktree collection
at all (measured: 'engine speaks v1.6, manifest pins v1.5', UNSIGNALLED).
This control instead loads `{gate}` directly as a fake submodule of the
real, already-on-sys.path `lib.project_next` package (the same technique
controls/project-next-dependencies uses), so its relative imports resolve
to the repository's current `models.py`/`config.py` rather than an
archived pre-fix pair, and the CLI (and its version pin) is never invoked.
limits: Covers ONLY the log-only failure path of _parse_worktrees, via a deterministic injected CommandRunner - not a real corrupted git repository, and not the status-failure path (controls/project-next covers that with a real broken worktree).

cases.name: bad-log-unreadable
cases.why: Status succeeds and reports a tracked change; only `git log` raises. A known-dirty worktree must retain its dirty evidence rather than reading as unexamined.

cases.name: good-log-readable
cases.why: Both status and log succeed cleanly; a genuinely clean worktree must not be flagged.

anchors.why: The module as it stood immediately before #1488 (one try/except covering both status and log). On the known-bad input, its except resets status too, losing the already-successful dirty read (dirty=None, MISSES the known-bad input). On the known-good input it agrees with the current gate (dirty=False).
